pool.text: The modern name appears for the first time in the Gaelic period.
The Glasgow Fair began during this medieval period.
John Stewart left an endowment for St Mungo's Bell.
The University of Glasgow was founded adjoining the cathedral.
Glasgow University was founded as the second oldest university in Scotland.
The 14 incorporated trade crafts federated as the Glasgow Trades House.
Motorcycle speedway racing was first introduced to Glasgow at Ashfield Stadium.
Hampden Park set the European record for attendance at a football match.
Celtic won the European Cup final during a dual European final appearance.
The Burrell Collection and a campaign were launched to boost tourism.
Glasgow became the European Capital of Culture.
The St Mungo Museum of Religious Life and Art opened in Glasgow.
Strathclyde Region was abolished and the city regained full local government responsibility.
Glasgow Hawks RFC was formed by the merger of two oldest clubs.
A Poet Laureate post was created for Edwin Morgan.
Glasgow was given the title of European Capital of Sport.
Glasgow had the lowest life expectancy of any UK city.
The city's primary airport was the target of a terrorist attack.
The Clydeside Distillery opened in the former dock pump house.
The sewerage infrastructure was improved with a long storm water tunnel.
